draft_only.results:

draft_only.title: HERO-63867 - API Portal - Can not generate a negative check with MSSQL env
1. Negative Check Generation via API (MSSQL)
1.1. Generate Negative Check with Valid YYYYMMDD Business Date
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Infrasys POS system is configured and running in an MSSQL database environment.
2. Valid API Portal access credentials and authentication tokens are available.
3. The station is online and successfully connected to the MSSQL database.
draft_only.steps:
1. Authenticate with the API Portal and obtain a valid session token.
2. Construct the API request payload for the "Generate a negative check" endpoint.
3. Set the "businessdate" parameter strictly to the YYYYMMDD format (e.g., 20260827).
4. Send the POST request to the API endpoint.
draft_only.results:
1. The system successfully processes the request without throwing any SQL Exceptions.
2. A negative check is generated successfully and recorded in the MSSQL database.
3. The API returns a 200 OK status code along with the generated check details.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Generate Negative Check with Invalid Business Date Format
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Infrasys POS system is configured and running in an MSSQL database environment.
2. Valid API Portal access credentials and authentication tokens are available.
draft_only.steps:
1. Authenticate with the API Portal and obtain a valid session token.
2. Construct the API request payload for the "Generate a negative check" endpoint.
3. Set the "businessdate" parameter to an invalid format (e.g., YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YYYY).
4. Send the POST request to the API endpoint.
draft_only.results:
1. The system rejects the request and does not generate a check.
2. The API returns a 400 Bad Request status with a clear validation error message regarding the incorrect date format.
3. No SQL Exception or database error is logged in the system station logs.

draft_only.title: 1.3. Generate Negative Check with Missing Business Date Parameter
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Infrasys POS system is configured and running in an MSSQL database environment.
2. Valid API Portal access credentials and authentication tokens are available.
draft_only.steps:
1. Authenticate with the API Portal and obtain a valid session token.
2. Construct the API request payload for the "Generate a negative check" endpoint.
3. Completely omit the "businessdate" parameter from the request payload.
4. Send the POST request to the API endpoint.
draft_only.results:
1. The system rejects the request due to missing mandatory parameters.
2. The API returns a 400 Bad Request status indicating the "businessdate" field is required.
3. The system remains stable without any database connection errors or SQL Exceptions.
2. API Response and Data Validation

draft_only.title: 2.1. Verify Successful Response Payload Structure
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Infrasys POS system is configured and running in an MSSQL database environment.
2. A valid negative check generation request payload is prepared.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a valid "Generate a negative check" API request with a correctly formatted YYYYMMDD business date.
2. Capture the HTTP response from the API Portal.
3. Inspect the JSON response body structure and data types.
draft_only.results:
1. The response status code is 200 OK.
2. The response body contains all expected fields, including check number, amount, business date, and transaction status.
3. The data types in the response payload strictly match the API specification documentation.

draft_only.title: 2.2. Verify System Behavior with Invalid Check Amount
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Infrasys POS system is configured and running in an MSSQL database environment.
2. Valid API Portal access credentials and authentication tokens are available.
draft_only.steps:
1. Construct the API request payload for the "Generate a negative check" endpoint.
2. Set a valid YYYYMMDD "businessdate".
3. Set the check amount to an invalid format (e.g., alphanumeric characters like "ABC").
4. Send the POST request to the API endpoint.
draft_only.results:
1. The system rejects the request due to invalid amount formatting.
2. The API returns a 400 Bad Request status indicating an invalid amount value.
3. No check is generated in the database, and no SQL Exception occurs.

draft_only.title: HERO-64092 - API Portal - POSgAPI - Add Check Owner in GET /checks/{{checkNo}} endpoint response for closing user (POS Dev)
Functional Testing
1. API Response Structure and Backward Compatibility
1.1. Verify new field presence and data type in single check endpoint
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Infrasys POS API Portal is accessible and authenticated.
2. Valid shopCode, outletCode, and checkNo parameters are available.
3. An active check exists in the system.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a GET request to the endpoint /shops/{shopCode}/outlets/{outletCode}/checks/{checkNo}.
2. Inspect the returned JSON response payload.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns a 200 OK success status.
2. The response payload includes the new field "check_owner_employee_no".
3. The data type of the "check_owner_employee_no" field is strictly a string.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Verify new field presence and data type in table checks endpoint
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Infrasys POS API Portal is accessible and authenticated.
2. Valid shopCode, outletCode, and tableNo parameters are available.
3. At least one check is currently assigned to the specified table.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a GET request to the endpoint /shops/{shopCode}/outlets/{outletCode}/tables/{tableNo}/checks.
2. Inspect the returned JSON response payload for all checks associated with the table.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns a 200 OK success status.
2. Every check object within the response array includes the "check_owner_employee_no" field.
3. The data type of the "check_owner_employee_no" field for each check is strictly a string.

draft_only.title: 1.3. Verify backward compatibility of existing response payload
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A baseline JSON schema of the previous API response version is available.
2. Valid API parameters are prepared for both check and table endpoints.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send GET requests to both /checks/{checkNo} and /tables/{tableNo}/checks endpoints.
2. Compare the new response payloads against the baseline JSON schema.
draft_only.results:
1. All previously existing fields and their data structures remain completely unchanged.
2. The new "check_owner_employee_no" field is added additively without breaking the existing schema.
3. No existing fields are removed, renamed, or altered in data type.
2. Check Ownership and Tip Attribution Logic

draft_only.title: 2.1. Verify check owner when opened by Digital Dine with no transfer
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A check is opened via the Digital Dine service user (e.g., employee number 9099).
2. No POS user has taken ownership of the check yet.
draft_only.steps:
1. Call the GET /checks/{checkNo} endpoint for the Digital Dine check.
2. Extract the "check_owner_employee_no" and "open_employee_no" fields from the response.
draft_only.results:
1. The "check_owner_employee_no" field is populated and not empty.
2. The value of "check_owner_employee_no" matches the Digital Dine service user's employee number (e.g., "9099").
3. The value matches the "open_employee_no" field.

draft_only.title: 2.2. Verify check owner when POS user takes ownership from Digital Dine
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A check is initially opened by the Digital Dine service user.
2. A POS user (e.g., employee number 100001) explicitly takes check ownership via the POS interface.
draft_only.steps:
1. Call the GET /checks/{checkNo} endpoint for the transferred check.
2. Extract the "check_owner_employee_no" and "open_employee_no" fields.
draft_only.results:
1. The "check_owner_employee_no" field returns the POS user's employee number (e.g., "100001").
2. The "open_employee_no" field remains unchanged as the original Digital Dine user (e.g., "9099").
3. The system correctly identifies the POS user as the current check owner for tip attribution.

draft_only.title: 2.3. Verify check owner updates correctly upon multiple ownership transfers
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A check is opened by User A.
2. User B takes ownership of the check.
3. User C subsequently takes ownership of the check from User B.
draft_only.steps:
1. Call the GET /checks/{checkNo} endpoint after the final transfer to User C.
2. Extract the "check_owner_employee_no" field.
draft_only.results:
1. The "check_owner_employee_no" field returns User C's employee number.
2. The field accurately reflects the most recent owner who explicitly took check ownership prior to closing.
3. Check Status and Workflow Coverage

draft_only.title: 3.1. Verify field inclusion across different check statuses
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Three checks exist in the system: one Open, one Closed, and one Voided.
2. All checks have valid check owner employee numbers assigned.
draft_only.steps:
1. Call the GET /checks/{checkNo} endpoint for the Open check and verify the field.
2. Call the endpoint for the Closed check and verify the field.
3. Call the endpoint for the Voided check and verify the field.
draft_only.results:
1. The "check_owner_employee_no" field is present and correctly populated in the Open check response.
2. The field is present and correctly populated in the Closed check response.
3. The field is present and correctly populated in the Voided check response.

draft_only.title: 3.2. Verify field persistence across various POS operational workflows
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. API endpoints for Send check, Park order, Retrieve park order, Edit item, and Split and pay are accessible.
2. A valid check is available for workflow testing.
draft_only.steps:
1. Execute a Send check and retrieve the response.
2. Execute a Park order by table and retrieve the response.
3. Execute an Edit item and retrieve the response.
4. Verify the "check_owner_employee_no" field in all returned payloads.
draft_only.results:
1. The "check_owner_employee_no" field is consistently included in the response for Send check.
2. The field is consistently included in the response for Park order and Retrieve park order.
3. The field is consistently included in the response for Edit item and Split and pay workflows.
4. Edge Cases and Negative Scenarios

draft_only.title: 4.1. Verify field value when assigned user lacks an employee number
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A POS user account is created in User Management without a User No. (employee number) configured.
2. This user takes ownership of an open check.
draft_only.steps:
1. Call the GET /checks/{checkNo} endpoint for the check owned by the user without an employee number.
2. Inspect the "check_owner_employee_no" field in the response.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns a 200 OK success status.
2. The "check_owner_employee_no" field is present in the payload.
3. The value of "check_owner_employee_no" is an empty string, as per the system fallback logic for users without a configured number.

draft_only.title: 4.2. Verify API error handling for invalid identifiers
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Valid authentication tokens are available.
2. Invalid or non-existent shopCode, outletCode, checkNo, and tableNo parameters are prepared.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a GET request to /checks/{checkNo} using a non-existent checkNo.
2. Send a GET request to /tables/{tableNo}/checks using a non-existent tableNo.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns the appropriate 404 Not Found or 400 Bad Request error status for the invalid checkNo.
2. The API returns the appropriate error status for the invalid tableNo.
3. The error responses do not contain the "check_owner_employee_no" field and maintain standard error payload structures.

draft_only.title: HERO-65043 - Unlock Table function causes an integrity problem when the check is under Send/Merge processes
Functional Testing
1. Table Merge and Unlock Concurrency
1.1. Verify Workstation B cannot unlock Table 1 during an ongoing merge process
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Two workstations (Workstation A and Workstation B) are logged into the POS system.
2. Table 1 and Table 2 are available and unlocked.
draft_only.steps:
1. Create a check on Table 1 with multiple line items.
2. Create a check on Table 2 with multiple line items.
3. On Workstation A, initiate the merge table function to merge Table 2 into Table 1 and confirm.
4. While Workstation A displays the loading screen for the merge process, immediately attempt to unlock Table 1 on Workstation B.
draft_only.results:
1. The system blocks the unlock table function on Workstation B.
2. Table 1 remains locked, and no integrity issues occur in the check data.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Verify Workstation B can unlock Table 1 after the merge timeout period
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Two workstations (Workstation A and Workstation B) are logged into the POS system.
2. Table 1 and Table 2 are available and unlocked.
3. merge_table_time is set to a short duration (e.g., 10 seconds) in config.ini for testing purposes.
1. Two workstations (Workstation A and Workstation B) are logged into the POS system.
2. Table 1 is available and unlocked.
draft_only.steps:
1. Create a check on Table 1 with multiple line items.
2. Create a check on Table 2 with multiple line items.
3. On Workstation A, initiate the merge table function to merge Table 2 into Table 1 and confirm.
4. Wait for the configured merge_table_time duration to elapse.
5. Attempt to unlock Table 1 on Workstation B.
1. Create a check on Table 1 with multiple line items.
2. On Workstation A, open the check on Table 1 and initiate the send check process.
3. While Workstation A is processing and displaying the loading screen for the send function, attempt to unlock Table 1 on Workstation B.
draft_only.results:
1. The system successfully allows Workstation B to unlock Table 1.
2. Table 1 status changes to unlocked without causing any data integrity issues.
2. Verify Workstation B cannot unlock Table 1 during an ongoing send process
1. The system blocks the unlock table function on Workstation B.
2. Table 1 remains locked until the send process is fully completed, ensuring data integrity.
3. Configuration and Timeout Validation

draft_only.title: 3.1. Verify the merge_table_time configuration correctly dictates the lock duration
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Access to the server file system where the POS configuration is stored.
2. Two workstations (Workstation A and Workstation B) are logged into the POS system.
draft_only.steps:
1. Open the file DRIVE/infrasys/local/hero_pos/cfg/config.ini.
2. Add or edit the line merge_table_time = 15 under the [setup] section.
3. Save the file and restart the POS application if required.
4. On Workstation A, initiate a merge table function for a table with multiple line items.
5. Attempt to unlock the table on Workstation B at 10 seconds and then at 20 seconds.
draft_only.results:
1. At 10 seconds, the system blocks the unlock function on Workstation B.
2. At 20 seconds, the system allows the unlock function on Workstation B.

draft_only.title: 3.2. Verify default timeout behavior when merge_table_time is not defined
draft_only.prerequisites:

2. Two workstations (Workstation A and Workstation B) are logged into the POS system.
draft_only.steps:

3. Save the file and restart the POS application if required.
4. On Workstation A, initiate a merge table function for a table with multiple line items.
5. Attempt to unlock the table on Workstation B at 300 seconds and then at 370 seconds.
draft_only.results:
1. At 300 seconds, the system blocks the unlock function on Workstation B.
2. At 370 seconds (exceeding the default 360 seconds), the system allows the unlock function on Workstation B.

correctly, and the failure alert email is successfully sent to the Email Group configured in Fail Notification.

draft_only.title: HERO-66793 - POS Interface – Enhance the General V3 Points Redemption function to support input by points value (Dev 3/3)
Functional Testing
1. Configuration and Setup
1.1. Configure Redeem Point Value Code for All Locations
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Access the Infrasys POS platform with administrative privileges.
2. Ensure the General v3 membership interface is already configured.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to POS System > Interface Configurations > Payment Settings.
2. Click "Add New" to configure a new setup.
3. Set "Apply To" to "All Locations".
4. Set "Interface" to "General v3 interface".
5. Enter a valid target value in the "Redeem Point Value Code" field.
6. Fill in the remaining required details and click "Save".
draft_only.results:
1. The setup record is successfully saved without errors.
2. The configuration is correctly applied and visible across all locations.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Configure Redeem Point Value Code for Specific Scope
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Access the Infrasys POS platform with administrative privileges.
2. Ensure specific Shops, Outlets, or Stations are created in the system.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to Payment Settings and click "Add New".
2. Set "Apply To" to "Shop", "Outlet", or "Station".
3. Select the specific target Shop, Outlet, or Station from the dropdown.
4. Set "Interface" to "General v3 interface" and enter the "Redeem Point Value Code".
5. Click "Save" to save the record.
draft_only.results:
1. The setup record is successfully saved.
2. The configuration is strictly restricted to the selected specific Shop, Outlet, or Station.
2. Get Points API and Initial Display

draft_only.title: 2.1. Successful Get Points API with "Points" Type
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Open a printed check with a member attached.
2. Select a payment method attached with the General v3 membership interface and payment type "By Redeem Point".
draft_only.steps:
1. Click the "Paid" function to go to the cashier panel.
2. Select the target payment method to trigger the "Get Points" API.
3. Mock the external party to return a successful response where one of the "points[].type" equals "Points" with a corresponding "points[].price".
draft_only.results:
1. The system successfully retrieves the "points[].price" as the point amount.
2. The system displays the input box for the redeem amount with the message "Please input redeem point amount".

draft_only.title: 2.2. Successful Get Points API without "Points" Type
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Open a printed check with a member attached.
2. Select the target payment method.
draft_only.steps:
1. Click "Paid" and select the payment method to trigger the "Get Points" API.
2. Mock the external party to return a successful response where none of the "points[].type" equals "Points", but "points[0].price" is provided.
draft_only.results:
1. The system follows the existing workflow to retrieve "points[0].price" (the first one).
2. The input box is displayed correctly with the message "Please input redeem point amount".

draft_only.title: 2.3. Get Points API Timeout or Error Response
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Open a printed check with a member attached.
2. Select the target payment method.
draft_only.steps:
1. Click "Paid" and select the payment method to trigger the "Get Points" API.
2. Mock the external party to return a connection timeout or an error response.
draft_only.results:
1. The system prompts an appropriate error message.
2. The action of adding the payment to the cashier is aborted, and the workflow ends.

draft_only.title: 2.4. Get Points API Success but No Point Amount Returned
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Open a printed check with a member attached.
2. Select the target payment method.
draft_only.steps:
1. Click "Paid" and select the payment method to trigger the "Get Points" API.
2. Mock the external party to return a successful response but without any "points[].price" provided.
draft_only.results:
1. The system prompts the specific error message "No point amount returned".
2. The action is aborted, and the workflow ends.
3. Input Switching and Validation

draft_only.title: 3.1. Default Display and Switch to Points Input
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The "Get Points" API is successful.
2. The "Redeem Point Value Code" is configured and contains a non-empty value.
draft_only.steps:
1. Observe the initial display showing the redeem amount input box and the button "Or switch to Points".
2. Click the "Or switch to Points" button.
3. Observe the UI changes on the screen.
draft_only.results:
1. The input box swaps to point value with an empty default value.
2. The message changes to "Please input number of Points used for this redemption".
3. The button changes to "Or switch to monetary value".

draft_only.title: 3.2. Default Display without Switch Option
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The "Get Points" API is successful.
2. The "Redeem Point Value Code" setup does not exist or is empty.
draft_only.steps:
1. Click "Paid" and select the payment method.
2. Observe the input screen displayed by the system.
draft_only.results:
1. The system displays the input box for the redeem amount with the message "Please input redeem point amount".
2. The "Or switch to Points" button is NOT displayed on the screen.

draft_only.title: 3.3. Switch Back to Monetary Value
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. The screen is currently displaying the "Points" input mode.
draft_only.steps:
1. Click the "Or switch to monetary value" button.
2. Observe the UI changes on the screen.
draft_only.results:
1. The input box swaps back to the redeem amount input.
2. The message changes back to "Please input redeem point amount".
3. The button changes back to "Or switch to Points".

draft_only.prerequisites: 1. The input screen is displayed in either monetary or points mode.

draft_only.results:
1. The system prompts an error message indicating invalid input.
2. The system stays on the input box page without proceeding to the API call.

draft_only.steps: 1. Click the "Cancel" button on the input screen.

Step(s):

2. Navigate to the Payment Settings and configure the Redeem Point Value Code.

1. The UI elements (input boxes, switch buttons) render correctly without layout issues.
2. The workflow executes without UI glitches or functional errors.

1. Log in to the POS system on both browsers.
2. Perform the points redemption workflow, including input validation and error prompts.
3. Verify the display of messages and button states.

1. The layout and functionality remain consistent across Firefox and Edge.
2. All pop-ups, error messages, and input switches work as expected.

draft_only.title: HERO-66794 - POS Configuration - Align Menu Management Import/Export functions between Standalone HQ and Config Zones HQ
Functional Testing
1. Groupings Tab and UI Alignment
1.1. Verify Groupings Tab Visibility in Standalone HQ
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Standalone HQ environment is set up and accessible.
2. The environment is confirmed to NOT be in Enterprise mode.
draft_only.steps:
1. Log in to the Standalone HQ system.
2. Navigate to "Menu Management" -> "Import and Export".
3. Observe the available tabs at the top of the module.
draft_only.results:
1. The "Groupings" tab is successfully displayed alongside existing tabs.
2. The "Recipes" tab is also displayed as expected per the release notes.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Verify UI Layout and Field Behavior Consistency
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Standalone HQ environment is accessible.
2. The "Groupings" tab is visible in the Import/Export module.
draft_only.steps:
1. Click on the "Groupings" tab.
2. Observe the type selection dropdown, field layouts, and overall UI structure.
3. Compare the interface with the existing Config Zones HQ design.
draft_only.results:
1. The type selection logic and dropdown options match the Config Zones HQ design.
2. UI layout, field behaviors, and file format handling remain consistent with Config Zones HQ.
2. Item Department and Menu Department Import & Export

draft_only.title: 2.1. Export Item Department and Menu Department Data
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. Standalone HQ contains existing Item Department and Menu Department data.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to "Menu Management" -> "Import and Export".
2. Select the "Groupings" tab.
3. Select "Item Department" from the type selection and click "Export".
4. Select "Menu Department" from the type selection and click "Export".
5. Check the designated download directory for the exported files.
draft_only.results:
1. Item Department data is exported successfully as a compressed file.
2. Menu Department data is exported successfully.
3. Files are saved in the correct directory format matching Config Zones HQ.

draft_only.title: 2.2. Import Item Department and Menu Department Data
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Exported files for Item Department and Menu Department are available from the previous test case.
2. Target standalone HQ system is ready for data import.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to the "Groupings" tab in the target system.
2. Select "Item Department", upload the corresponding exported file, and click "Import".
3. Select "Menu Department", upload the corresponding exported file, and click "Import".
4. Verify the imported data in the Menu Management module.
draft_only.results:
1. Item Department data is imported successfully without errors.
2. Menu Department data is imported successfully.
3. Data reflects correctly in the system, and new records are created if the target system does not exist.
3. Item Category and Menu Category Import & Export

draft_only.title: 3.1. Export Item Category and Menu Category Data
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. Standalone HQ contains existing Item Category and Menu Category data.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to "Menu Management" -> "Import and Export".
2. Select the "Groupings" tab.
3. Select "Item Category" from the type selection and click "Export".
4. Select "Menu Category" from the type selection and click "Export".
draft_only.results:
1. Item Category data is exported successfully.
2. Menu Category data is exported successfully.
3. File formats and structures match Config Zones HQ standards.

draft_only.title: 3.2. Import Item Category and Menu Category Data
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. Exported files for Item Category and Menu Category are available.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to the "Groupings" tab.
2. Select "Item Category", upload the file, and click "Import".
3. Select "Menu Category", upload the file, and click "Import".
4. Check for changes upon importing in the system.
draft_only.results:
1. Item Category data is imported and updated correctly.
2. Menu Category data is imported and updated correctly.
3. No data corruption or mapping errors occur during the process.
4. Existing Import/Export Functions Regression

draft_only.title: 4.1. Verify Items and Menus Import/Export Functions
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. Standalone HQ contains existing Items and Menus data.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to "Menu Management" -> "Import and Export".
2. Select the "Items" tab, perform an export and an import operation.
3. Select the "Menus" tab, perform an export and an import operation.
draft_only.results:
1. Items export and import functions normally without any regression or UI changes.
2. Menus export and import functions normally without any regression or UI changes.

draft_only.title: 4.2. Verify General Tag, Recipes, and Not For Sale Items Import/Export
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. Standalone HQ contains existing General Tag, Recipes, and Not For Sale Items data.
draft_only.steps:
1. Select the "General Tag" tab and perform export/import operations.
2. Select the "Recipes" tab and perform export/import operations.
3. Select the "Not For Sale Items" tab and perform export/import operations.
draft_only.results:
1. General Tag functions remain completely unaffected.
2. Recipes functions remain unaffected and operate as expected.
3. Not For Sale Items functions remain completely unaffected.
5. Validation and Edge Cases

draft_only.title: 5.1. Validate File Format and Validation Logic for Groupings
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Standalone HQ is accessible.
2. An invalid file (e.g., .txt format or corrupted zip file) is prepared.
draft_only.steps:

2. Select a grouping type (e.g., Item Department).
3. Upload the invalid file.
4. Click "Import".
draft_only.results:
1. System successfully rejects the invalid file.
2. An appropriate error message is displayed to the user.
3. Validation logic remains strictly consistent with the existing Config Zones HQ implementation.

draft_only.title: 5.2. Verify Feature Availability in Enterprise Mode

2. Navigate to "Menu Management" -> "Import and Export".
3. Check for the presence and availability of "Groupings" and "Recipes" tabs.
draft_only.results:
1. "Groupings" and "Recipes" tabs are hidden or disabled in Enterprise mode.
2. System correctly enforces the non-Enterprise mode restriction as outlined in the release notes.

draft_only.results:
1. The report displays a single combined section aggregating all selected periods.
2. The data matches the current POS008 output for the same period selection without period-based grouping.
2. Breakdown by Period Enabled with Multiple Meal Periods (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner)
1. The report displays a separate section for each selected period in the system-configured order (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner).
2. Each section is headed by the configured meal period name.
3. Each section contains only transactions whose check was opened during that specific period, including accurate sales quantities, revenue, and cost.
4. All period sections appear consecutively on the same page, separated by a heading or divider line.
5. A grand total section is appended at the end, correctly aggregating all fields across all selected periods.
3. Breakdown by Period Enabled with Single Meal Period (Breakfast)
1. The report displays a single section for the Breakfast period.
2. The data is identical to the current POS008 output for the same single period.
3. No grand total section is displayed.
4. Parameter Reset Behavior on Screen Reopen
1. The "Breakdown by Period" parameter successfully resets to Disabled, regardless of its previous state.
5. Transaction Assignment Based on Check Open Time
1. The test transaction appears exclusively in the Breakfast section.
2. The transaction does not appear in the Lunch section, confirming assignment is based on check open time.
Report Functional Verification
1. Export to CSV, Excel, and Excel (.xlsx)
1. Each exported file displays the period-separated layout mirroring the on-screen preview.
2. Period headings, per-period data sections, and the grand total section are correctly formatted and populated in all three file types.
2. Export to PDF, Word, PostScript, and PowerPoint (.pptx)
1. Each exported file retains the period-separated layout, including period headings and the grand total section.
2. Page breaks and dividers are correctly applied across all formats without truncating period data.
3. Print to HTML and PDF
1. The HTML and PDF print outputs accurately reflect the period-separated layout and grand total section.
2. Formatting, headers, and dividers are correctly rendered in both print formats.
4. Create, Edit, and Run Preset Parameters
1. The preset parameter is successfully created and saved.
2. The preset parameter is successfully edited.
3. Running the report via the preset parameter generates the correct period-separated layout based on the updated configuration.
5. Auto Run Preset Parameters to Email, FTP, and SFTP
1. The reports are successfully delivered to Email, FTP, and SFTP.
2. The attached/uploaded files contain the correct period-separated layout and grand totals.
6. Multi-language Support Verification
1. The "Breakdown by Period" parameter label is correctly translated.
2. The meal period names in the report headers are displayed in the selected language.
3. The period-separated layout and grand total section function correctly in the secondary language.
7. Format Configuration and Auto Report Configuration Settings
1. The custom format configurations are correctly applied to the period-separated sections and grand total.
2. The auto-generated report successfully applies the "Breakdown by Period" logic without manual intervention.
Report Compatibility Verification
1. Browser Compatibility (Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
1. The report criteria screen and on-screen preview render consistently across all three browsers.
2. Export functions perform correctly without UI glitches or layout breaks in Chrome, Firefox, and Edge.
2. POS Client Compatibility (Windows, Android, iOS)
1. Transactions from Windows, Android, and iOS POS clients are correctly captured and assigned to their respective meal period sections.
2. No data discrepancies are observed based on the POS client operating system.
3. Config Zone Compatibility
1. The report correctly displays only the meal periods configured for the specific Config Zone.
2. Period headings and data sections accurately reflect the zone-specific meal period configurations.
4. Data Service Compatibility (MySQL, TiDB, MSSQL)
1. The report generates identical period-separated layouts and grand total values across MySQL, TiDB, and MSSQL.
2. No performance degradation or query errors occur with the new grouping logic on any of the supported databases.

draft_only.title: HERO-67160 - POS Interface - PMS - Shiji Template 1 - Allow browsing the returned result on enquiry screen (Dev)
Functional Testing
1. Enquiry Workflow with Setup 1 Enabled (Show Basic Info = Yes)
1.1. Verify PMS enquiry screen displays results and Confirm button
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Infrasys Cloud POS is configured with an HTNG PMS interface.
2. The interface setup "Show Basic Information In Payment Workflow" (Setup 1) is set to "Yes".
3. A printed check is available in the system.
draft_only.steps:
1. Open the printed check.
2. Click the "Paid" function to navigate to the cashier screen.
3. Select the HTNG PMS interface payment having the payment type "Room".
4. Input valid search criteria on the PMS enquiry screen.
5. Click the "Room Enquiry" button.
draft_only.results:
1. The system successfully triggers the external API for PMS enquiry.
2. The system displays the enquiry result and automatically selects the first guest in the result list.
3. The "Confirm" button is visible on the screen at the correct position based on the PMS type.
4. The basic information of the initially selected guest is displayed.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Verify guest details update when selecting a different guest
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The PMS enquiry screen is displayed with multiple guest results.
2. Setup 1 is set to "Yes".
draft_only.steps: 1. Click on a different guest in the result list (not the first one).
draft_only.results:
1. The newly selected guest is highlighted in the result list.
2. The system updates and displays the basic information and details of the newly selected guest.

draft_only.title: 1.3. Verify payment confirmation via Confirm button or double-click
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The PMS enquiry screen is displayed with results.
2. A specific guest is selected and their details are visible.
3. Setup 1 is set to "Yes".
1. Infrasys Cloud POS is configured with an HTNG PMS interface.
2. The interface setup "Show Basic Information In Payment Workflow" (Setup 1) is set to "No".
3. A printed check is available in the system.
1. HTNG PMS interfaces are configured for Standard, Shiji, Shiji Template 1, and ShijiConnect+ types.
2. Setup 1 is set to "Yes" for all configured interfaces.
draft_only.steps:
1. Click the "Confirm" button to finalize the selection.
1. Open the printed check and click "Paid" to go to the cashier screen.
2. Select the HTNG PMS interface payment with payment type "Room".
3. Input search criteria and click the "Room Enquiry" button.
4. Select another guest in the result list.
1. Perform the Room Payment enquiry workflow for the "Standard" PMS type and verify the UI.
2. Repeat the workflow for the "Shiji" PMS type and verify the UI.
3. Repeat the workflow for the "Shiji Template 1" PMS type and verify the UI.
4. Repeat the workflow for the "ShijiConnect+" PMS type and verify the UI.
draft_only.results:
1. The system closes the PMS enquiry screen.
2. The system successfully uses the selected guest for the PMS room payment.
3. (Alternative validation: Clicking on the target guest a second time also successfully confirms the selection and proceeds to payment).
2. Verify Confirm button is hidden and guest is directly selected when Setup 1 is No
1. The system displays the enquiry result and selects the first guest.
2. The "Confirm" button is completely hidden from the UI.
3. Upon selecting another guest in the result list, the system directly uses the newly selected guest for the PMS payment without requiring any additional confirmation step.
3. Verify enquiry workflow across Standard, Shiji, Shiji Template 1, and ShijiConnect+ PMS types
1. The enquiry workflow, result display, and "Confirm" button functionality work correctly for all four supported PMS types.
2. The position of the "Confirm" button renders appropriately according to the specific UI layout requirements of each PMS type.
4. Edge Cases and Negative Scenarios

draft_only.title: 4.1. Verify system behavior when PMS enquiry returns no results
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The PMS enquiry screen is open.
2. Setup 1 is set to "Yes".
draft_only.steps:
1. Input invalid or non-existent search criteria.
2. Click the "Room Enquiry" button.
draft_only.results:
1. The system triggers the API and returns an empty result list.
2. No guest is selected in the list.
3. The "Confirm" button is disabled or hidden, preventing invalid payment confirmation.
4. An appropriate message is displayed indicating no guests were found.

draft_only.title: 4.2. Verify system behavior when external PMS API fails
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The PMS external API is mocked to return a failure or timeout.
2. The PMS enquiry screen is open.
draft_only.steps:
1. Input valid search criteria.
2. Click the "Room Enquiry" button.
draft_only.results:
1. The system handles the API failure gracefully without crashing.
2. An error message is displayed to the user indicating the enquiry failed.
3. The system allows the user to retry the enquiry or cancel the operation.

draft_only.title: HERO-67175 - POS Interface - Email Alert for fail of portal station (Dev)
1. Configuration and Setup
1.1. Verify successful configuration of POS Monitor Tools and Fail Notification
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. User is logged in to the Infrasys POS platform with administrative privileges.
2. The HKJC module is installed and the server type is set to Mix or Slave mode.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to System Management -> System Configuration -> HKJC Module.
2. Click "Edit" to configure the settings.
3. Under the "Monitor Tool Settings" section, locate "POS Monitor Tools".
4. Click "<<< Edit Configuration >>>" to open the "Monitor Tool Configuration" dialog.
5. Under "Basic Configuration", set "POS Launcher Service Monitor Enable" to "Enable".
6. Set "Fail Notification" to a valid "Target Email Group".
7. Click "Continue" and then click "Save" to save the record.
draft_only.results:
1. The "Monitor Tool Configuration" dialog opens successfully without errors.
2. The system saves the configuration successfully and returns to the main HKJC Module settings page.
3. Re-opening the configuration dialog reflects the updated "Enable" status and the selected Target Email Group.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Verify validation for invalid or missing Email Group in Fail Notification
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. User is logged in with administrative privileges.
2. The "Monitor Tool Configuration" dialog is open.
draft_only.steps:
1. Ensure "POS Launcher Service Monitor Enable" is set to "Enable".
2. Leave the "Fail Notification" field blank or attempt to enter an invalid/non-existent email group name.
3. Click "Continue" and then click "Save".
draft_only.results:
1. The system prevents the save action and displays a validation error message indicating that a valid Target Email Group is required.
2. The configuration is not saved, and the previous valid settings (if any) remain intact.
2. Email Alert Triggering and Logic

draft_only.title: 2.1. Verify immediate email alert when a single portal station goes down
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. POS Monitor Tools is configured and enabled with a valid Target Email Group.
2. The POS Service Monitor Shell background job is active and running.
3. All portal stations are currently in a "Running" state.
draft_only.steps:
1. Stop or simulate the failure of a single portal station.
2. Wait for the POS Service Monitor Shell background job to execute its next scheduled run.
3. Check the inbox of the configured Target Email Group.
draft_only.results:
1. An email alert is sent immediately upon the background job detecting the downed portal station, with no waiting period or delay.
2. The email content accurately identifies and includes the details of the single portal station that is not running.

draft_only.title: 2.2. Verify consolidated email alert when multiple portal stations go down
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. POS Monitor Tools is configured and enabled with a valid Target Email Group.
2. Multiple portal stations are currently in a "Running" state.
draft_only.steps:
1. Stop or simulate the failure of multiple portal stations simultaneously, or sequentially before the next background job run.
2. Wait for the POS Service Monitor Shell background job to execute.
3. Check the inbox of the configured Target Email Group.
draft_only.results:
1. Only one consolidated email is sent for that specific background job run.
2. The email includes the details of all portal stations that are not running at the time of execution, rather than sending individual emails for each station.

draft_only.title: 2.3. Verify email re-triggering in subsequent runs if station remains down
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A portal station has been stopped and an initial alert email has been successfully sent.
2. The portal station remains in a "Not Running" state.
draft_only.steps:
1. Allow the POS Service Monitor Shell background job to execute subsequent runs while the portal station is still down.
2. Monitor the inbox of the Target Email Group.
draft_only.results:
1. An email alert is triggered again for each subsequent background job run where the portal station is detected as not running.
2. The background job evaluates the need to add the email job independently for every run, ensuring continuous alerts for unresolved outages.

draft_only.title: 2.4. Verify no duplicate or delayed email alerts when portal station recovers
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A portal station is down and failure alerts have been triggered.
2. The background job is actively running.
draft_only.steps:
1. Restart the portal station so it returns to a "Running" state.
2. Wait for the next background job run to complete.
3. Check the email inbox of the Target Email Group.
draft_only.results:
1. No "recovery" or "service restored" email alerts are sent, as the requirement strictly defines alerts for failures.
2. No further "down" email alerts are triggered for the recovered station in the subsequent background job run.

draft_only.title: 2.5. Verify email alert behavior when server type is not Mix or Slave mode
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The HKJC module is installed, but the server type is set to a mode other than Mix or Slave (e.g., standalone).
2. POS Monitor Tools is configured and enabled with a valid Target Email Group.
draft_only.steps:
1. Stop a portal station to simulate a failure.
2. Wait for the POS Service Monitor Shell background job to execute.
3. Check the inbox of the Target Email Group.
draft_only.results:
1. The email alert feature is not triggered, correctly aligning with the requirement that it is only available for HKJC modules with server types set to Mix or Slave mode.
2. No email is sent to the Target Email Group.

draft_only.title: HERO-67311 - POS Interface - KDS2.0 - Add authorization token and enhance exisiting API for Infrasys KDS 2.0 interface (POS Dev)
Functional Testing
1. Interface Setup and Configuration
1.1. Verify addition of new authentication setups and removal of deprecated setups
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Log in to the Infrasys POS Platform with administrative privileges.
2. Navigate to Interface Control > Interfaces.
draft_only.steps:
1. Click "Add New" to configure a new Shiji KDS interface.
2. Select Interface Type = Kitchen Display System (KDS) and Vendor = Shiji KDS.
3. Review the "Connection Setup" section fields.
4. Review the "General Setup" section fields.
5. Save the configuration.
draft_only.results:
1. "Tenant Id", "Client Id", and "Client Secret" fields are successfully displayed under Connection Setup.
2. The "custom_passcode" grant type setup is removed.
3. Setup 5 (setting of passcode) and Setup 6 (setting of device UID) are successfully removed.
4. The setup previously named "Posting language for name" is correctly updated to "Posting Language For Name".
5. The new setup "Language Code To Internal Language Index Mapping" is available under General Setup.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Verify "Language Code To Internal Language Index Mapping" configuration
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. A Shiji KDS interface is created and saved.
draft_only.steps:
1. Edit the existing Shiji KDS interface record.
2. Locate the "Language Code To Internal Language Index Mapping" field.
3. Input the mapping values: "1:en" and "2:zh-hk".
4. Click "Save" to save the record.
5. Trigger a posting event that utilizes multi-language names.
draft_only.results:
1. The mapping configuration is saved successfully without validation errors.
2. POS internal language index 1 correctly maps to the i18n language code 'en'.
3. POS internal language index 2 correctly maps to the i18n language code 'zh-hk'.
4. The posted API payload correctly reflects the mapped language codes for the corresponding names.
2. Authorization Token Management

draft_only.title: 2.1. Verify successful access token retrieval using client_credentials
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A Shiji KDS interface is configured with valid Tenant Id, Client Id, and Client Secret.
2. The KDS Auth API is accessible and responding.
draft_only.steps:
1. Trigger an interface posting event from the POS.
2. Monitor the outgoing network requests and system logs.
3. Verify the token validity period.
draft_only.results:
1. The POS successfully sends a request to the KDS Auth API using the client_credentials grant type.
2. The access token is successfully retrieved and cached by the system.
3. The retrieved token is configured with a 24-hour validity time.

draft_only.title: 2.2. Verify token refresh mechanism with 60-second buffer
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. An access token is cached and nearing its expiration time.
2. Mock the token expiration to be exactly 59 seconds away.
draft_only.steps:
1. Trigger an interface posting event.
2. Monitor the token management logs and outgoing requests.
draft_only.results:
1. The system detects that the token expires in 59 seconds (which is 60 seconds or less).
2. The system automatically triggers the refresh token API before executing the posting event.
3. The token is successfully refreshed and the posting event proceeds with the new token.

draft_only.title: 2.3. Verify fallback to new token retrieval if refresh fails
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The KDS Auth API refresh token endpoint is mocked to return a failure/error response.
2. An access token is cached and nearing expiration.
draft_only.steps:
1. Trigger the token refresh mechanism.
2. Monitor the system logs and outgoing requests.
draft_only.results:
1. The refresh token request fails as expected.
2. The system automatically falls back and requests a completely new access token using the client_credentials grant type.
3. The new access token is successfully obtained and cached for subsequent postings.

draft_only.title: 2.4. Verify system behavior when authentication credentials are empty
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Edit the Shiji KDS interface setup.
2. Leave "Tenant Id", "Client Id", or "Client Secret" fields empty.
3. Save the configuration.
draft_only.steps:
1. Trigger an interface posting event.
2. Check the system logs and outgoing network requests.
draft_only.results:
1. The system does not post any request to get or refresh the authorization token.
2. The posting event is halted or fails gracefully.
3. Corresponding error logs are accurately recorded in the system indicating missing credentials.
3. API Header Enhancements

draft_only.title: 3.1. Verify access token and tenant ID in API headers for all endpoints
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A valid access token is successfully retrieved and cached.
2. The Shiji KDS interface is fully configured and activated.
draft_only.steps:
1. Execute the following operations in POS to trigger the respective APIs: Void ticket, Update ticket information, Update ticket items, Rush ticket, Change table, Create new ticket, Add pantry message, and Merge table.
2. Intercept and inspect the outgoing HTTP headers for all 8 API calls.
draft_only.results:
1. All 8 specified API endpoints successfully include the access token in the authorization header.
2. All 8 specified API endpoints successfully include the Tenant ID in the header.
3. The headers are correctly formatted according to the KDS 2.0 API Swagger specifications.
4. API Body Enhancements and Multi-language Support

draft_only.title: 4.1. Verify updated API body and multi-language support for ticket types, items, and menus
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Multi-language mapping is configured in the interface setup.
2. Menu items, courses, and ticket types are created with multiple language translations in the POS.
1. Log in to the Infrasys POS Platform with administrative privileges.
2. One Shiji KDS interface is already configured and activated on the local server.
draft_only.steps:
1. Trigger "Create new ticket", "Update ticket information", "Update ticket items", and "Add pantry message" operations.
2. Intercept and inspect the JSON body payloads of the outgoing API requests.
1. Navigate to Interface Control > Interfaces.
2. Click "Add New" to configure a second Shiji KDS interface.
3. Attempt to activate the second Shiji KDS interface.
4. Observe the system behavior and validation messages.
draft_only.results:
1. The API body for "Update ticket information" includes multi-language ticket type names and the corresponding ticket type code.
2. The API body for "Update ticket items" includes multi-language item names.
3. The API body for "Create new ticket" includes multi-language menu names, and the menu name field is correctly marked as required.
4. The API bodies correctly include multi-language support for Course Names and Pantry Messages based on the configured language index mapping.
5. Verify only one Shiji KDS interface can be activated per local server
1. The system prevents the activation of the second Shiji KDS interface.
2. An appropriate validation message or error is displayed indicating that only one Shiji KDS interface can be configured and activated on a single local server.
3. The first interface remains active and unaffected.

draft_case.title: 2.1. Verify first-time pantry message triggers notification when disabled
draft_case.prerequisites:
1. The "Allow Repeated Pantry Message Hook Notification" setup is set to "No" or does not exist.
2. An API Hook is subscribed to the pantrymessage.add event.
draft_case.steps:
1. Open an existing check in the POS.
2. Click the "Pantry Message" function.
3. Select a target item that does not currently have a pantry message.
4. Click the "Confirm" button.
5. Select a target pantry message (e.g., "Rush").
6. Monitor the API Hook logs for the pantrymessage.add event.
draft_case.results:

draft_only.title: HERO-67545 - Printing Core Service - Make printer connect retry and status monitoring interval configurable via config.ini
Functional Testing
1. Configuration Loading and Application
1.1. Verify default values are applied when config.ini uses default settings
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The config.ini file is present but the [printer] section is either missing or contains only the default values (connect_timeout_ms=500, connect_retry_count=5, status_regular_check_interval_ms=2000, enable_stagger_status_check_start=1).
2. The Printing Core Service is currently stopped.
draft_only.steps:
1. Start the Printing Core Service.
2. Open the application logs and verify the loaded configuration parameters.
3. Simulate a printer connection failure and observe the retry behavior.
4. Monitor the printer status polling mechanism over a 10-minute period.
draft_only.results:
1. The service starts successfully without any errors.
2. Logs correctly display the default effective values: 500ms timeout, 5 retries, 2000ms interval, and stagger enabled.
3. The system attempts to reconnect exactly 5 times with a 500ms delay between each attempt.
4. The system polls the printer status every 2000ms (2 seconds) consistently.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Verify custom values are applied for busy-site configuration
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The config.ini file is updated with busy-site recommended values under the [printer] section: connect_timeout_ms=1000, connect_retry_count=20, status_regular_check_interval_ms=300000, enable_stagger_status_check_start=1.
2. The Printing Core Service is currently stopped.
draft_only.steps:
1. Start the Printing Core Service.
2. Open the application logs and verify the loaded configuration parameters.
3. Simulate a printer connection failure and observe the retry behavior.
4. Monitor the printer status polling mechanism over a 15-minute period.
draft_only.results:
1. The service starts successfully without any errors.
2. Logs correctly display the custom effective values: 1000ms timeout, 20 retries, 300000ms interval, and stagger enabled.
3. The system attempts to reconnect exactly 20 times with a 1000ms delay between each attempt (totaling ~20 seconds of retry time).
4. The system polls the printer status exactly every 300000ms (5 minutes).
2. Fallback and Error Handling

draft_only.title: 2.1. Verify fallback to defaults when parameters are missing
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The config.ini file contains the [printer] section, but specific keys (e.g., connect_retry_count and status_regular_check_interval_ms) are completely removed.
2. The Printing Core Service is currently stopped.
draft_only.steps:
1. Start the Printing Core Service.
2. Check the application logs for the effective configuration values.
3. Verify the operational behavior of the missing parameters.
draft_only.results:
1. The service starts successfully without crashing or throwing fatal errors.
2. The logs indicate that the missing parameters have fallen back to their default values (5 for retry count, 2000 for interval).
3. The system behaves exactly as it would with the default configuration for the missing parameters.

draft_only.title: 2.2. Verify fallback to defaults when parameters contain invalid data types
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The config.ini file is updated with invalid data types for the parameters (e.g., connect_timeout_ms=abc, connect_retry_count=-5, status_regular_check_interval_ms=null).
2. The Printing Core Service is currently stopped.
draft_only.steps:
1. Start the Printing Core Service.
2. Check the application logs for warnings and effective configuration values.
3. Verify the operational behavior of the system.
draft_only.results:
1. The service starts successfully and does not fail.
2. The logs display warnings regarding the invalid values and confirm fallback to default values for the affected parameters.
3. The system operates normally using the default values for the invalid parameters.

draft_only.title: 2.3. Verify fallback to defaults when parameters are empty
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The config.ini file is updated with empty values for the parameters (e.g., connect_timeout_ms=, connect_retry_count=).
2. The Printing Core Service is currently stopped.
draft_only.steps:
1. Start the Printing Core Service.
2. Check the application logs for the effective configuration values.
3. Verify the system startup status.
draft_only.results:
1. The service starts successfully without interruption.
2. The logs confirm that empty parameters are treated as invalid and fall back to their respective default values.
3. No exceptions or crashes occur during the initialization phase.
3. Logging and Startup Behavior

draft_only.title: 3.1. Verify effective configuration values are logged at startup
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The config.ini file is configured with a mix of valid custom values and default values.
2. The Printing Core Service is currently stopped.
draft_only.steps:
1. Start the Printing Core Service.
2. Navigate to the service log directory.
3. Open the latest startup log file and search for the printer configuration initialization block.
draft_only.results:
1. The service initializes and writes to the log file successfully.
2. The log file contains a clear, readable summary of all 4 printer parameters.
3. The logged values exactly match the effective values applied by the system (custom where provided, defaults where missing/invalid).
4. Printer Connection and Status Monitoring Behavior

draft_only.title: 4.1. Verify printer connection retry behavior with custom timeout and retry count
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The config.ini is set to connect_timeout_ms=1000 and connect_retry_count=3 for testing purposes.
2. A network printer is physically disconnected or its IP is blocked to force connection failures.
draft_only.steps:
1. Trigger a print job or force a printer connection attempt via the POS interface.
2. Use a network monitoring tool or check the service logs to track the connection attempts.
3. Measure the time elapsed between each retry attempt.
draft_only.results:
1. The system attempts to connect to the printer exactly 3 times.
2. The time interval between each retry attempt is consistently measured at approximately 1000ms.
3. After the 3rd failed attempt, the system correctly marks the printer as offline/unavailable.

draft_only.title: 4.2. Verify staggered status check start behavior
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The config.ini is set with enable_stagger_status_check_start=1.
2. Multiple printers (at least 3) are configured in the system.
draft_only.steps:
1. Restart the Printing Core Service.
2. Monitor the exact timestamps of the very first status check for each configured printer in the logs.
3. Calculate the time differences between the initial status checks of the different printers.
draft_only.results:
1. The first status checks for the printers do not occur at the exact same millisecond.
2. The start times are randomized/staggered across the printers.
3. This prevents a synchronized network spike when polling multiple printers simultaneously.

draft_only.title: HERO-67651 - TMS 2.0 - Notification with Whatsapp - Dev (9/9)
1. Vendor and Interface Configuration
1.1. Verify WhatsApp Vendor and Interface Setup
draft_only.prerequisites:

2. Meta Cloud API credentials (API URL, Business ID, Access Token, Business Phone ID) are available.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to Messaging Control > Vendors.
2. Verify that the WhatsApp vendor is available in the vendor list.
3. Navigate to Messaging Control > Interfaces and click Add.
4. Select 'WhatsApp' as the interface type.
5. Enter the Meta Cloud API credentials and save the interface.
draft_only.results:
1. WhatsApp vendor is successfully displayed in the Vendors list.
2. WhatsApp interface is created successfully without errors.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Verify WhatsApp Interface Test Send Functionality
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A valid WhatsApp interface is configured with correct Meta Cloud API credentials.
2. An approved WhatsApp template is available in Meta.
draft_only.steps:
1. Navigate to Messaging Control > Interfaces and edit the WhatsApp interface.
2. Click 'Test Send WhatsApp'.
3. Select an approved template from the dropdown.
4. Fill in the required test variables and enter a valid recipient phone number.
5. Click Send.
draft_only.results:
1. The system successfully fetches and displays the list of active approved templates from Meta.
2. The test message is sent successfully, and a success confirmation is displayed.

draft_only.title: 1.3. Verify Debug Mode Logging for WhatsApp Interface

2. Access to the server file system (tmp/logs/) is available.
draft_only.steps:

2. Perform a Test Send WhatsApp and check the tmp/logs/ directory.
3. Disable Debug mode in the interface settings.
4. Perform another Test Send WhatsApp and check the tmp/logs/ directory.
draft_only.results:

draft_only.results:

draft_only.results:

2. Saving without updating mappings fails or warns the user; saving with correct mappings succeeds.

draft_only.title: 5.2. Verify Message Job Statuses and Retry Mechanism
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. A WhatsApp message job is configured with Retry Times, Retry Delay, and Expiry Time.
draft_only.steps:
1. Trigger a WhatsApp message job that encounters a retryable error (e.g., network timeout).
2. Observe the job status in msg_jobs and the retry behavior.
3. Trigger a job that encounters a non-retryable error (e.g., HTTP 400).
4. Observe the job status.
draft_only.results:
1. For retryable errors, the job status remains 'Wait for Handling' and reschedules after the Retry Delay until Retry Times/Expiry is reached (then becomes 'Timeout').
2. For non-retryable errors, the job status immediately becomes 'Fail'.

draft_only.title: 5.3. Verify Multiple Recipients Handling in WhatsApp Message Jobs
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. A reservation has multiple phone numbers configured, separated by semicolons.

draft_only.results:

draft_only.title: HERO-67661 - TMS2.0 - Create pending reservation task for third party payment through Open API (3/3)
1. Create Pending Reservation API
1.1. Create Pending Reservation with Valid Parameters and Custom Effective Time
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A "Partner Collected Payment" type interface payment is configured in the Admin page.
2. Valid shop code and outlet code are available.
3. The guest quota is not fully booked for the target date and time.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a POST request to /shops/{shopCode}/outlets/{outletCode}/pending_reservations with a valid JSON body.
2. Include the third_party object in the deposit JSON with a custom effective_time (e.g., 30 minutes) and a valid action_time.
3. Verify the API response status and payload.
4. Check the backend database for the newly created pending task record.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns a 200 OK status with a successfully generated pending_resv_id.
2. The pending task is created in the system, and the expiry time is correctly calculated as action_time + effective_time.
3. The guest quota is successfully deducted and counted for the pending reservation.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Create Pending Reservation using Default Interface Payment Expiry Time
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A "Partner Collected Payment" type interface payment is configured with a default expiry time of 15 minutes.
2. Valid shop code and outlet code are available.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a POST request to /shops/{shopCode}/outlets/{outletCode}/pending_reservations with a valid JSON body.
2. Omit the effective_time parameter in the third_party deposit JSON.
3. Verify the API response and the calculated expiry time in the backend.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns a 200 OK status with the pending_resv_id.
2. The pending task expiry time is correctly calculated using the interface payment's default expiry time (15 minutes) added to the action_time.

draft_only.title: 1.3. Validate Error Handling for Missing Mandatory Fields
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Valid shop code and outlet code are available.
2. API authentication secret key is configured.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a POST request to the pending reservations endpoint.
2. Omit mandatory fields such as date, time, adults, last_name, or deposit fields like amount, payment_code, payment_ref.
3. Observe the API error response.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns an error response with the corresponding error code (e.g., missing_date, missing_amount, missing_payment_ref).
2. The pending reservation is not created in the system.

draft_only.title: 1.4. Validate Error Handling for Duplicate Payment Reference
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. A pending reservation has already been successfully created with payment_ref = "REF12345".
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a POST request to the pending reservations endpoint using the exact same payment_ref = "REF12345".
2. Verify the API error response.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns an error with the code duplicate_payment_ref.
2. The system prevents the creation of a duplicate pending reservation.

draft_only.title: 1.5. Validate Restriction of Multiple Third-Party Payment Deposits
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. Valid shop code and outlet code are available.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a POST request to the pending reservations endpoint.
2. Include multiple deposit elements in the new JSON array (e.g., two third-party payment deposits).
3. Verify the API error response.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns an error with the code must_provide_only_one_new_third_party_payment_deposit.
2. The system enforces the restriction of only one pending third-party payment deposit per reservation.
2. Confirm Pending Reservation API

draft_only.title: 2.1. Confirm Pending Reservation to Normal Reservation Successfully
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A valid pending reservation exists with status "pending".
2. The pending reservation has not expired.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a PUT request to /shops/{shopCode}/outlets/{outletCode}/pending_reservations/{{pendingResvId}}.
2. Provide the correct date, payment_ref, and third_party.action_time in the request body.
3. Verify the API response and the reservation status in the backend.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns a 200 OK status with the normal reservation confirm_no and status "normal".
2. The pending task is converted to a normal reservation in the database.
3. If a confirmation notification is configured, the notification is successfully triggered and sent.

draft_only.title: 2.2. Validate Error Handling for Mismatched Payment Reference
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. A valid pending reservation exists with payment_ref = "REF12345".
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a PUT request to the confirm pending reservation endpoint.
2. Provide a mismatched payment_ref (e.g., "REF99999") in the request body.
3. Verify the API error response.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns an error with the code payment_ref_mismatch.
2. The pending reservation remains in "pending" status and is not converted.

draft_only.title: 2.3. Validate Error Handling for Expired Pending Task
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. A pending reservation exists but has exceeded its calculated expiry time.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a PUT request to the confirm pending reservation endpoint with valid parameters.
2. Verify the API error response.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns an error with the code pending_task_is_expired.
2. The system prevents the confirmation of an expired pending task.
3. Delete Pending Reservation API

draft_only.title: 3.1. Delete Pending Reservation with Valid Parameters
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A valid pending reservation exists.
2. The third-party payment has been cancelled via the edit reservation API first (if applicable).
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a DELETE request to /shops/{shopCode}/outlets/{outletCode}/pending_reservations/{{pendingResvId}}?date={{date}}&payment_ref={{payment_ref}}.
2. Provide the exact pendingResvId, date, and payment_ref used during creation.
3. Verify the API response and the backend database.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns a 200 OK status with success: true.
2. The pending reservation record is successfully deleted from the system.
3. The previously deducted guest quota is released back to the available pool.

draft_only.title: 3.2. Validate Error Handling for Invalid Encrypted Pending Task ID
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. Valid shop code and outlet code are available.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a DELETE request to the delete pending reservation endpoint.
2. Provide a malformed or incorrectly encrypted pendingResvId in the URL path.
3. Verify the API error response.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns an error with the code invalid_pending_resv_id (Decryption failed).
2. No records are deleted from the system.
4. Edit Reservation and Update Payment Status API

draft_only.title: 4.1. Update Third-Party Payment Status from Pending to Success
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. A normal reservation exists with a third-party payment deposit in "pending" status.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a PUT request to /shops/{shopCode}/outlets/{outletCode}/reservations/{confirmNo}.
2. In the deposits.edit array, set the third_party.status to "success" and provide the action_time.
3. Verify the API response and the payment records in the backend (tms_resv_payment, tms_payment_gateway_records, tms_payment_gateway_transactions).
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns a 200 OK status.
2. The payment status is successfully updated to "success" across all relevant payment tables.

draft_only.title: 4.2. Update Third-Party Payment Status from Success to Refund
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. A normal reservation exists with a third-party payment deposit in "success" status.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a PUT request to the edit reservation endpoint.
2. In the deposits.edit array, set the third_party.status to "refund" (indicating full refund, rpay_type = r).
3. Verify the API response and the backend payment records.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns a 200 OK status.
2. The payment status is updated to "refund" and rpay_type is set to "r" in the database.

draft_only.title: 4.3. Validate Invalid Payment Status Change Order
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. A normal reservation exists with a third-party payment deposit in "success" status.
draft_only.steps:
1. Send a PUT request to the edit reservation endpoint.
2. Attempt to change the third_party.status from "success" back to "pending".
3. Verify the API error response.
draft_only.results:
1. The API returns an error with the code invalid_status_change.
2. The system enforces the valid status change order and prevents reverting from success to pending.
5. Background Job and Quota Management

draft_only.title: 5.1. Auto-Expire Pending Reservation and Release Quota via Background Job
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The "HERO TMS Update Pending Task Status" background job is configured and running.
2. A pending reservation exists and has exceeded its expiry time limit.
draft_only.steps:
1. Wait for the background job execution cycle to trigger.
2. Check the system logs and the backend database for the pending task status.
3. Verify the guest quota availability for the specific date and time.
draft_only.results:
1. The background job successfully identifies the expired pending reservation.
2. The pending reservation status is automatically updated to "expired" or deleted.
3. The guest quota previously held by the pending reservation is successfully released.

draft_only.title: TMS2.0 - Rebranding - New login page for Profile Management Test Report
Functional Testing
1. Login Page Branding Display
1.1. Default Profile Management login page shows the new branded UI
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The Infrasys POS build containing the rebranding changes is deployed.
2. No custom login background image has been configured yet.
draft_only.steps:
1. Open the Profile Management login page.
2. Check the product name, product logo, module name, and default background image.
3. Log in with valid credentials and check the general page header after login.
draft_only.results:
1. The Profile Management login page uses the same login UI as the Admin login page.
2. The product name shows "Infrasys POS" instead of "Infrasys Cloud" and the new product logo is displayed on the login page and the general page header.
3. The module name "Profile Management" is shown on the login page.
4. The default login background image is the same one used by the Admin login page.

draft_only.title: 1.2. Login with valid and invalid credentials on the new login page
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. A valid Profile Management user account exists.
2. The Profile Management login page is accessible.
draft_only.steps:
1. Enter a valid username and password on the new login page and click Login.
2. Log out, then enter an invalid username or password and click Login.
draft_only.results:
1. Login with valid credentials succeeds and navigates to the Profile Management home page.
2. Login with invalid credentials fails and an error message is displayed on the new login page.
2.Custom Login Background Image Configuration

draft_only.title: 2.1. Admin configures the login background via Global Settings
draft_only.prerequisites: 1. Administrator account has access to System Management > System Configuration.
draft_only.steps:
1. Go to System Management > System Configuration > Global Settings.
2. Edit the Custom Login Background Image, upload a new image, and save.
3. Open the Profile Management login page.
draft_only.results:
1. The custom background image is saved successfully.
2. The Profile Management login page displays the uploaded background image.

draft_only.title: 2.2. Member Module configuration updates the login background
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Administrator account has access to System Management > System Configuration.
2. A custom background image has already been set in Global Settings.
draft_only.steps:
1. Go to System Management > System Configuration > Member Module.
2. Edit the Custom Login Background Image with a different image and save.
3. Open the Profile Management login page.
draft_only.results:
1. The member module background image is saved successfully.
2. The Profile Management login page displays the image configured in the Member Module.

draft_only.title: 2.3. Sub config zone overrides the background image in Enterprise mode
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The system is running in Enterprise mode with a sub config zone that has an active Shop.
2. A background image is configured in the current config zone global setting.
draft_only.steps:
1. In the sub config zone, override the Custom Login Background Image with its own image and save.
2. Open the Profile Management login page of that sub config zone.
draft_only.results:
1. The background image override for Profile Management is supported in the sub config zone.
2. The sub config zone login page uses its own background image.

draft_only.title: 2.4. Background image fallback precedence chain
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Enterprise mode with a sub config zone, a current config zone, and the Supreme Config Zone are available.
2. Background images can be configured at each level independently.
draft_only.steps:
1. Clear the background image of the sub config zone and open its Profile Management login page.
2. Clear the current config zone global setting background image and open the login page again.
3. Clear the member module background image of the Supreme Config Zone and open the login page again.
4. Clear the Supreme Config Zone global setting background image and open the login page again.
draft_only.results:
1. With no sub config zone image, the login page falls back to the background image of the current config zone global setting.
2. With no current config zone global setting image, the login page falls back to the background image of the member module of the Supreme Config Zone.
3. With no Supreme member module image, the login page falls back to the background image of the Supreme Config Zone global setting.

draft_only.title: 3.1. Authentication can be enabled for Profile Management login
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. Administrator account has access to the authentication configuration.
2. The Profile Management login page is accessible.
draft_only.steps:
1. Enable the Authentication option for Profile Management login and save.
2. Open the Profile Management login page and log in with valid credentials.
draft_only.results:
1. Profile Management login supports enabling Authentication.
2. Login behaves according to the enabled authentication setting.

draft_only.title: 3.2. Password reset is supported from Profile Management login
draft_only.prerequisites:
1. The Profile Management login page is accessible.
2. A user account with an email address exists for password reset.
1. Administrator account has access to System Management > System Configuration and Audit Logs Management > Audit Logs.
draft_only.steps:
1. On the Profile Management login page, trigger the Reset Password flow with the user account email.
2. Complete the reset process and log in with the new password.
1. Go to System Management > System Configuration > Global Settings, modify the Custom Login Background Image, and save.
2. Go to Audit Logs Management > Audit Logs and view the audit log.
draft_only.results:
1. Profile Management login supports resetting the password.
2. The user can log in successfully with the new password.
4.Audit Log for Background Image Modification
1. After the background image is modified and saved successfully, an audit log is generated.
2. The audit log details reflect the background image modification.

1. Admin login page and its default background image display.
2. General page header logo and product name across other modules.
3. Normal Profile Management login and logout flows.
4. Other System Configuration settings editing and saving.
5. Audit log generation for other configuration changes.
